title: SSN Media Fellowship 2026-2027 for Scholars New to Media Engagement: Apply for Personalized Media Training, Mentorship, and Public Communication Support
summary: The Scholars Strategy Network (SSN) has announced applications for the 2026-2027 SSN Media Fellowship, an exclusive professional development opportunity designed to support scholars who are interested in expanding their ability to communicate research findings through media platforms. The fellowship is created specifically for SSN members who are new to media engagement and want to develop the skills needed to effectively share research with wider audiences. Through personalized mentorship, practical media workshops, and guidance from experienced public scholars and SSN national staff, selected fellows will gain valuable tools for engaging with journalists, producing impactful public scholarship, and increasing the visibility of their research. Applications for the SSN Media Fellowship 2026-2027 must be submitted by September 21, 2026. About the SSN Media Fellowship The SSN Media Fellowship is entering its fourth year and continues Scholars Strategy Network’s commitment to helping researchers become stronger public communicators. The program recognizes that important research findings often have the potential to influence public discussions, policies, and communities, but many scholars may need additional support to effectively communicate their work beyond academic audiences. This fellowship provides selected SSN members with the opportunity to receive personalized guidance from experienced scholars who have successfully engaged with media outlets and public audiences. Participants will learn how to communicate their research through different media channels, including: Television interviews Radio discussions Print media Opinion articles and op-eds Digital media platforms Social media communication The fellowship is designed to help scholars develop practical media strategies and build confidence when interacting with journalists, policymakers, and the public. Fellowship Benefits and Support Provided Selected fellows will receive a combination of mentorship, training, and individualized support throughout the 2026-2027 academic year. The program includes: 1. Personalized Mentorship From Experienced Public Scholars Each selected fellow will be paired with an experienced public scholar from the Scholars Strategy Network membership. Mentors will provide practical advice, feedback, and guidance on developing effective media engagement strategies. Mentor-mentee relationships will focus on helping fellows identify opportunities to communicate their research and strengthen their public presence. Mentorship pairs are expected to meet approximately five times during the fellowship period. 2. Media Training Workshops In addition to mentorship, fellows will participate in media workshops organized by SSN national staff. These workshops will provide training and practical knowledge on topics such as: Understanding how the media works Communicating academic research clearly to non-academic audiences Developing effective media messages Preparing for interviews Writing compelling opinion pieces Building relationships with journalists and media professionals 3. Tailored Support From SSN National Staff SSN staff will provide additional assistance throughout the fellowship, including: Reviewing and editing op-ed drafts Supporting media pitches Helping fellows identify relevant media contacts Sharing media opportunities and alerts Providing guidance on effective communication strategies This support is designed to help fellows successfully translate their research into meaningful public conversations. Important Note About Funding The SSN Media Fellowship does not provide a stipend or financial award to selected fellows. The main value of the program is the professional development, mentorship, training, and networking opportunities provided through participation. Eligibility Requirements for the SSN Media Fellowship To be considered for the fellowship, applicants must: Be current members of the Scholars Strategy Network Be interested in improving their media engagement skills Have research projects that can be communicated to public audiences Be relatively new to media work or looking to strengthen their existing media experience Be willing to participate actively in mentorship meetings and media workshops throughout the academic year Due to program limitations, applications are only accepted from current SSN members. Application Requirements Applicants must complete an online application form and provide the following information: Personal Information Applicants are required to submit: First name Last name Email address Research Project Description Applicants must provide a short description or abstract of the research project or projects that they would like to focus on during their media engagement activities. The research should be suitable for public communication and demonstrate potential value for broader audiences. Media Engagement Statement Applicants must submit a statement of between 500 and 1,000 words explaining: Their interest in media engagement Any previous media experience they have Their goals for participating in the fellowship How the fellowship will support their professional development Mentor-Mentee Meeting Interests Applicants should explain what they hope to explore during mentor meetings throughout the fellowship. This may include areas such as: Developing a media strategy Improving public communication skills Learning how to engage journalists Identifying opportunities for sharing research Receiving feedback on media-related projects Curriculum Vitae Applicants must provide a link to their most recent CV. The CV should highlight relevant academic, professional, research, and public engagement experiences. Additional Information Applicants may also share any additional information, ideas, or thoughts regarding potential mentor pairings. This section is optional but allows applicants to provide further context about their interests and goals. Read Full Details HERE SSN Media Fellowship 2026-2027 Timeline The fellowship will follow the schedule below: September 21, 2026 Application deadline. All applications must be submitted by this date. October 2026 Selected fellows will be notified and matched with mentors. All fellows will also participate in an onboarding session before beginning mentor meetings and media workshops. November 2026 The first media workshop led by SSN national staff will take place. Spring 2027 Fellows will participate in two additional media workshops led by SSN staff. June 2027 The fellowship program will officially conclude, followed by an evaluation of the program experience. Why Apply for the SSN Media Fellowship? The SSN Media Fellowship offers scholars an opportunity to move beyond traditional academic communication and connect their research with communities, decision-makers, and the wider public. By participating in this program, fellows can develop stronger communication skills, gain confidence in media engagement, receive personalized advice from experienced scholars, and learn strategies for making research more accessible and impactful. For researchers interested in increasing the reach and influence of their work, the fellowship provides a valuable platform for developing public scholarship skills. How to Apply Interested applicants should complete the official application form before the deadline. Apply HERE Applicants with questions may contact Dominik Doemer, Director of Communications at Scholars Strategy Network, through dominik@scholars.org. Conclusion The SSN Media Fellowship 2026-2027 is a valuable opportunity for Scholars Strategy Network members who want to strengthen their ability to communicate research through media and public platforms. Through expert mentorship, practical workshops, and personalized support, selected fellows will gain the knowledge and confidence needed to share important research findings with broader audiences. Eligible SSN members interested in developing their media engagement skills and expanding the public impact of their research are encouraged to submit their applications before the September 21, 2026 deadline. title: Safe Arborist Techniques Fund Grant Program 2026: Up to $15,000 Research Funding for Tree Safety, Arborist Innovation, Climbing Techniques, Rigging Systems, and Safer Tree Care Practices
summary: The Safe Arborist Techniques Fund (SATF) Grant Program 2026 is an important research funding opportunity supporting innovation, safety improvement, and knowledge development within the arboriculture and tree care industry. The program is jointly established by the Tree Research and Education Endowment Fund (TREE Fund) and the International Society of Arboriculture (ISA) to support research and development focused on improving the techniques, equipment, and safety practices used by arborists when climbing, rigging, and working with trees. Through this grant program, researchers and institutions are encouraged to develop evidence-based solutions that help create safer working environments for arborists while improving understanding of tree work risks, equipment performance, and hazard identification. The SATF Grant Program provides funding of up to $15,000 per project and expects funded projects to be completed within two years from the initial fund disbursement . About the Safe Arborist Techniques Fund (SATF) The tree care profession involves complex and physically demanding activities, including tree climbing, equipment operation, rigging, and managing hazardous situations. Arborists often work in environments where safety risks can arise from: Tree structure and stability Equipment limitations Rigging techniques Climbing methods Environmental conditions Human factors during tree operations The Safe Arborist Techniques Fund was created to support research that addresses these challenges and develops practical solutions that protect arborists and improve industry standards. The program focuses on advancing: Safer climbing techniques Improved rigging practices Better arborist equipment Hazard identification methods Workplace safety systems Evidence-based tree care practices Grant Benefits Successful applicants may receive: Research funding of up to $15,000 Support for innovative arboriculture safety research Opportunity to contribute to improved industry standards Platform to share findings with researchers and tree care professionals Opportunity to publish research outcomes in professional journals Recognition through TREE Fund research networks Funded researchers are expected to contribute knowledge that can benefit arborists, urban forestry professionals, researchers, and organizations involved in tree management. Areas of Research Supported TREE Fund welcomes research proposals from a broad range of academic and technical disciplines. Projects may involve: Qualitative research Quantitative research Engineering studies Safety assessments Equipment and technique evaluation Risk identification studies Arboriculture technology development Research should contribute to improving safety in areas such as: Tree climbing Rigging operations Arborist equipment Tree work procedures Hazard prevention Projects Not Eligible for Funding The SATF Grant Program does not support certain types of projects. Applications will not be accepted for: 1. Individual Grants The program does not provide grants directly to individuals. Funding must be connected to eligible research institutions or organizations. 2. Municipal Tree Surveys or Assessments Projects primarily focused on municipal tree inventories, surveys, or assessments are not eligible. 3. Tree Planting Programs Funding is not available for tree planting initiatives. 4. Traditional Forestry and Conservation Studies Projects focused mainly on: Forestry production Timber management Agroforestry Forest ecology Conservation of natural forests are not eligible. 5. Product Testing for Commercial Benefit Research focused primarily on testing a product for the benefit of the company manufacturing that product will not be funded. Application Timeline and Important Deadlines The SATF Grant application process follows a structured timeline. Letter of Intent (LOI) Period Opening Date: August 1, 2026 LOI Submission Deadline: September 1, 2026 TREE Fund will only accept Letters of Intent between August 1 and September 1, 2026. Proposal Review Notification September 15, 2026 Applicants whose Letters of Intent meet the requirements will be invited to submit a full proposal. Full Proposal Submission Deadline October 15, 2026 Only applicants whose LOIs are approved will be allowed to submit complete applications. Grant Recipient Notification Mid-to-late December 2026 Selected applicants will be informed of funding decisions. Application Process The application process consists of two major stages: Step 1: Submit a Letter of Intent (LOI) Applicants must first submit an LOI through the online application portal. The Letter of Intent must clearly identify: Principal Investigator (PI) Institution responsible for conducting the research Research concept Alignment with SATF priorities TREE Fund reviews each LOI to determine whether: The project meets eligibility requirements The research aligns with program goals The project has reasonable potential for success Only approved LOIs move forward to the full application stage. Step 2: Submit Full Research Proposal Applicants invited after LOI approval must submit a complete proposal by: October 15, 2026 The full proposal must provide detailed information about the research project, methodology, budget, and expected outcomes. Application Requirements Applicants must provide information about: Principal Investigator Co-Principal Investigators Student assistants (if applicable) Curriculum vitae information The proposal must include the following sections: 1. Project Description Overall Project Summary (Maximum 400 words) Applicants must explain: The current problem being addressed The impact of the issue on arboriculture and urban forestry The goals of the proposed research 2. Measurable Outputs and Outcomes (Maximum 250 words) Applicants should describe: Expected research outputs Publications Educational materials Presentations Outreach activities Applicants should also identify up to five measurable outcomes showing how the research may improve tree care practices. 3. Current Knowledge and Previous Research (Maximum 1,000 words) This section should include: Existing knowledge about the research topic Previous attempts to address the problem Relevant scientific literature Experience of the research team 4. Project Work Plan (Maximum 1,500 words) Applicants must clearly explain: Research scope Research objectives Hypotheses Study design Methodology Data analysis approach Any commercial or proprietary elements 5. Dissemination Plan (Maximum 300 words) Applicants should explain how research findings will be shared with: Academic communities Arboriculture professionals Industry stakeholders TREE Fund encourages researchers to make findings widely available. 6. Literature References Applicants should provide relevant citations following recognized academic citation standards. Budget Requirements Applicants must provide detailed budget information, including: Eligible Budget Categories Institutional compensation Research stipends Employee benefits Travel expenses Transportation costs Equipment purchases Materials and supplies Contract labor Consultants Speakers Institutional overhead Other expenses Institutional overhead is limited to: Maximum 10% Applicants must also identify: Cash contributions from other sources In-kind support A minimum of: 10% additional funding support is required. Selection Criteria Applications are reviewed based on several important factors. TREE Fund reviewers will focus on: 1. Research Team Experience Reviewers consider: Previous achievements Research experience Expertise of investigators Early-career researchers are encouraged to collaborate with experienced researchers or advisors. 2. Contribution to Arboriculture Projects should demonstrate clear potential to improve: Arborist safety Tree care practices Industry knowledge 3. Research Approach Evaluation includes: Strength of research questions Experimental design Methodology Scientific quality 4. Dissemination Strategy Reviewers assess how effectively findings will reach: Researchers Tree care professionals Industry stakeholders Diversity and Inclusion Statement TREE Fund does not discriminate based on: Race Color Creed Gender Sexual orientation Disability National origin Ethnic background The organization welcomes applications from diverse researchers and institutions. However, current TREE Fund trustees and immediate family members of trustees are not eligible to receive grants. Award Process and Fund Distribution Grant recommendations are reviewed by the TREE Fund Research and Education Committee before being presented to the TREE Fund Board of Trustees. Grant approvals occur during: Spring Grants: May Board Meeting Fall Grants: December Board Meeting Recipients receive written notification within one month of trustee approval. Successful applicants must complete: Grant agreement forms Payment schedules Reporting requirements Required documentation Reporting Requirements TREE Fund expects research findings to be shared widely so they can benefit the arboriculture community. Grant recipients should: Notify TREE Fund when research findings are published Inform TREE Fund about conference presentations Acknowledge TREE Fund support in publications and presentations Share findings through professional journals Researchers are encouraged to publish in journals such as: Arboriculture and Urban Forestry Urban Forestry Urban Greening Arboricultural Journal Trees: Structure and Function Journal of Horticultural Science and Biotechnology Plant Pathology HortScience Sustainable Development Landscape and Urban Planning Journal of Urban Health Urban Ecosystems Previous Safe Arborist Techniques Fund Grant Recipients Examples of previously funded projects include: 2025 Award Leonardo Bianchini, PhD University of Tuscia Department of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences Project: “Tree Risk during Rigging Operations: Identifying Biomechanical Risk Factors for Arborist Safety – TRIAS” 2024 Award Lawrence Kahn Tulane Law School Utility Vegetation Management Institute Project: “Enhancing the ANSI Z133 Safety Standard’s Effectiveness with Case Studies” 2023 Award Lawrence Kahn Tulane Law School Utility Vegetation Management Institute Project: “Can Mandatory Minimum Clearance Requirements Between Trees and Powerlines Successfully Reduce Injuries and Death to Workers and the Public?” 2022 Award Dr. John Ball South Dakota State University Project: “Evaluation of Efficiencies Among Climbing Systems and Rope Diameters” 2019 Award Matt Follett Université du Québec à Montréal (UQAM) Project: “Evaluation of Load Distribution in Removal Operations: A Comparison of Techniques and Equipment” Read Full Details HERE How to Apply Interested applicants should prepare their research proposal and submit their Letter of Intent through the official TREE Fund application portal HERE Conclusion The Safe Arborist Techniques Fund Grant Program 2026 provides an excellent opportunity for researchers and institutions to advance safety, innovation, and scientific understanding within the arboriculture industry. By supporting research into climbing techniques, rigging systems, equipment improvement, and hazard prevention, the program contributes to creating safer workplaces for arborists worldwide. Researchers with strong proposals that can improve tree care safety practices are encouraged to submit their Letters of Intent before September 1, 2026 , and take part in developing the future of safer arboriculture. title: Erasmus Mundus Scholarships 2027 | Fully Funded Master’s Scholarships in Europe for International Students
summary: Applications for the prestigious Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarships 2027 are expected to open soon for international students worldwide. Funded by the European Union , these fully funded scholarships provide an opportunity to pursue a high-quality international master s degree while studying at multiple universities across Europe and beyond. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are among Europe s most prestigious international master s programmes. They are jointly designed and delivered by a consortium of leading universities from different countries, offering students a unique international learning experience, world-class education, and global career opportunities. Outstanding applicants may receive fully funded scholarships covering tuition, living expenses, travel, and visa costs. Unlike traditional master s programmes, Erasmus Mundus students typically study in at least two countries during their degree and graduate with either a joint degree or multiple degrees awarded by the participating universities. Whether you are interested in engineering, public health, climate change, data science, international development, business, law, artificial intelligence, or social sciences, the Erasmus Mundus Catalogue features hundreds of internationally recognised master s programmes taught in English. Key details Applications Expected to Open: October 2026 Host Countries: Europe (Study in multiple countries) Funded By: European Union (Erasmus+ Programme) Degree Level: Master s (Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters) Scholarship Coverage: Full tuition/participation costs Monthly living allowance Travel support Visa contribution Additional programme-related support (where applicable) Eligible Applicants: International students from all countries Programme Duration: 1–2 years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS) Application Deadline: Varies by programme (Most applications close between October and January) Apply Through: Individual Erasmus Mundus programme websites Applications for the prestigious Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarships 2027 are expected to open soon for international students from around the world. Funded by the European Union , these fully funded scholarships allow outstanding students to pursue a joint master s degree at some of Europe s top universities while studying in multiple countries. The Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM) programme is one of the world s most competitive international scholarship programmes, offering students a unique opportunity to earn a joint or multiple master s degrees through an integrated study programme delivered by a consortium of universities across Europe and beyond. Whether you re looking to advance your academic career, gain international experience, or build a global professional network, the Erasmus Mundus Scholarship is an excellent opportunity to study abroad with full financial support. Why Apply for Erasmus Mundus Scholarships? The Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters programme offers students the opportunity to: Study at multiple universities in different countries. Gain international academic and cultural experience. Receive a joint or multiple master s degree recognized worldwide. Learn from leading academics and industry experts. Participate in research projects, internships, traineeships, and thesis work depending on the programme. Build a strong international professional network. Programmes are jointly designed and delivered by at least three higher education institutions from three different countries , together with academic and industry partners. Erasmus Mundus Scholarship Benefits Outstanding applicants may receive a fully funded scholarship covering: Full participation or tuition costs Monthly living allowance Travel expenses Visa costs Installation and other eligible programme-related support Scholarship benefits are awarded directly by the selected Erasmus Mundus programme and may vary slightly depending on the consortium. Programme Duration Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters typically last: 1 year (60 ECTS) 1.5 years (90 ECTS) 2 years (120 ECTS) Students study at different partner universities throughout the programme and graduate with either: A Joint Master s Degree , or Multiple Master s Degrees issued by participating universities. Who Can Apply? Students from all countries worldwide are eligible to apply. Applicants must: Hold a bachelor s degree (or equivalent), or Be in their final year of undergraduate studies and graduate before the master s programme begins. Some programmes may have additional academic or language requirements depending on the field of study. Required Documents Application requirements vary by programme, but commonly include: Bachelor s degree certificate (or proof of final-year enrolment) Academic transcripts Curriculum Vitae (CV) Letter of Motivation or Statement of Purpose Letters of Recommendation Proof of English language proficiency (where required) Passport or national identification document Some programmes may also request: Research proposal Portfolio Relevant work experience Additional programme-specific documents Always check the official website of your chosen programme for the complete list of requirements. How to Apply for Erasmus Mundus Scholarships 2027 Unlike many scholarship programmes, there is no central Erasmus Mundus application portal . To apply: Visit the official Erasmus Mundus Catalogue. Search for programmes that match your academic background and interests. Visit the official website of your selected programme. Carefully review the admission requirements and scholarship criteria. Submit your application directly to the consortium running the programme before its deadline. Applicants should also contact the programme coordinators if they have questions regarding admissions or scholarship availability. When to Apply Most Erasmus Mundus Joint Master s programmes accept applications between October and January for programmes beginning the following academic year. Application deadlines differ for each programme, so applicants should regularly check the official programme website. Tips for a Strong Erasmus Mundus Application To improve your chances of receiving a scholarship: Maintain a strong academic record. Write a compelling and personalized motivation letter. Obtain high-quality recommendation letters. Highlight leadership, volunteer work, research, internships, and extracurricular achievements. Demonstrate how the programme aligns with your academic and career goals. Apply early and ensure all required documents are submitted before the deadline. Erasmus Mundus Scholarships in Numbers Since its launch, almost 50,000 students from around the world have participated in Erasmus Mundus programmes, making it one of Europe s most successful international scholarship initiatives. Application Deadline Varies by programme. Most scholarship applications close between October and January , although exact dates depend on each master s programme. Applicants should consult the official programme website for the latest deadlines. title: ACLS Digital Justice Grants 2026-27 | Up to $100,000 for Digital Scholarship Projects
summary: Applications are now open for the 2026-27 ACLS Digital Justice Grants Program , a funding opportunity designed to support innovative digital projects across the humanities and social sciences. Administered by the American Council of Learned Societies (ACLS) and generously funded by the Mellon Foundation, the program seeks to advance equitable and inclusive digital scholarship that critically engages with the histories, experiences, and interests of historically marginalized communities. The program offers both Seed Grants and Development Grants to scholars and research teams using ethical digital methods to expand access to knowledge, strengthen community engagement, and promote justice-centered approaches to digital humanities and social science research. About the ACLS Digital Justice Grants Program The ACLS Digital Justice Grants Program aims to address long-standing inequities in access to digital tools, resources, and institutional support within the humanities and interpretive social sciences. The initiative supports projects that center the experiences of historically marginalized communities, including but not limited to: * Black communities * Latinx communities * Indigenous communities * People with disabilities * Queer, trans, and gender nonconforming communities * Other historically underrepresented groups By funding innovative digital scholarship, ACLS seeks to promote inclusion, sustainability, and broader participation in the digital transformation of humanistic inquiry. Grant Categories Digital Justice Seed Grants Seed Grants are designed for projects in the early stages of development. Funding Amount : $10,000 – $25,000 These grants support: * Planning workshops * Prototype development * Testing new methodologies * Exploring innovative research agendas * Experimenting with new source materials and digital approaches Digital Justice Development Grants Development Grants support projects that have moved beyond the proof-of-concept stage and are ready for expansion. Funding Amount :$50,000 – $100,000 These grants support projects that: * Demonstrate significant preliminary work * Have evidence of scholarly or public engagement * Require resources for the next stage of development * Have clear plans for technological, intellectual, and financial sustainability What Types of Projects Are Supported ? The program supports projects that use digital tools and methods to advance justice-oriented scholarship and community engagement. Eligible activities include: * Ethical digital projects focused on historically marginalized communities * Capacity-building initiatives in digital humanities * Publicly engaged projects developed with community partners * Pedagogical initiatives that train students in digital humanities methods * Collaborative projects connecting scholars across institutions * Projects that develop new technological infrastructure for research and public engagement * Digital knowledge dissemination and content-building initiatives Additional Support for Grant Recipients In addition to grant funding, all recipients will have access to financial planning coaching provided by the Nonprofit Finance Fund. This support helps projects develop long-term sustainability strategies and stewardship plans beyond the grant period. Eligibility Criteria To apply, projects must meet the following requirements: * The Principal Investigator must be a scholar in the humanities or interpretive social sciences. * Awarded funds must be administered by a U.S. institution of higher education. * Projects should be made as openly accessible as intellectual property considerations allow. * Seed Grant applicants must be in the start-up or prototyping phase. * Development Grant applicants must demonstrate substantial prior work and public or scholarly impact. Ineligible Projects ACLS Digital Justice Grants do not support projects whose sole or primary focus is: * Creative works such as novels or films * Textbooks * Straightforward translations * Purely pedagogical projects Institutional indirect costs are also not covered under this funding opportunity. Grant Period Funded projects must begin between: July 1, 2027 and December 31, 2027 Projects may have a work plan lasting between 12 and 18 months. Webinar Series for Applicants To support prospective applicants, ACLS is hosting a series of webinars throughout the application period. Topics include: * General application guidance * Data ethics * Capacity building * Data stewardship * Insights from former reviewers and grantees The first information session is scheduled for: August 20, 2026 at 2:00 PM EDT How to Apply Applications must be submitted through the ACLS online fellowship and grant administration system . Applicants should review all program guidelines, eligibility requirements, FAQs, and supplementary materials before preparing their proposals. Complete applications must be submitted no later than November 3, 2026, at 5:00 PM ET . Conclusion The ACLS Digital Justice Grants 2026-27 represent a significant opportunity for scholars and research teams committed to advancing equity, inclusion, and justice through digital scholarship. With funding of up to $100,000, the program empowers researchers to develop innovative projects that preserve underrepresented histories, build community-centered digital resources, and expand access to knowledge across the humanities and social sciences. Whether you are launching a new digital initiative or scaling an established project, this funding opportunity can help transform your vision into lasting impact. Interested applicants are encouraged to begin preparing their applications early and take advantage of the webinar series and support resources offered by ACLS. title: Goals for Tomorrow 2026 in Canada | Call for Youth Presenters
summary: Are you a young leader, innovator, artist, activist, entrepreneur, researcher, or community builder making a positive impact in your community? If so, the Goals for Tomorrow 2026 festival is looking for youth presenters from across Canada to share their ideas, projects, experiences, and creative work with a national audience. Organized by Aga Khan Foundation Canada (AKFC) and The Students Commission of Canada , Goals for Tomorrow is a youth-led virtual festival that celebrates leadership, innovation, global citizenship, international development, and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). About Goals for Tomorrow 2026 Goals for Tomorrow: A Canadian Showcase of Youth Innovation will take place virtually on October 17, 2026 , bringing together young people from across Canada to explore solutions to social, environmental, and economic challenges. The festival provides a unique platform for youth to showcase their work, exchange ideas, and inspire others while contributing to meaningful conversations about creating a more sustainable and equitable future. Why Should You Present? Selected presenters will have the opportunity to: * Showcase their work to a national audience * Connect with youth changemakers from across Canada * Develop public speaking and leadership skills * Contribute to important conversations about social change * Receive recognition for their participation * Expand their professional and personal networks This is an excellent opportunity for young people who are passionate about community impact, innovation, sustainability, and youth leadership. Who Can Apply? The call is open to young people across Canada who are making a difference in their communities through leadership, innovation, creativity, advocacy, entrepreneurship, research, or community engagement. Whether you are leading a project, conducting research, creating art, launching a social enterprise, or advocating for change, Goals for Tomorrow welcomes your voice and perspective. Presentation Formats Applicants may submit proposals in one or more of the following formats: * TED-style talks * Interactive workshops * Panel discussions * Creative performances * Poetry and spoken word presentations * Photography showcases * Visual arts exhibitions * Film and video screenings * Peer-learning sessions * Social innovation case studies The festival encourages diverse and creative approaches to sharing ideas and experiences. Benefits of Participating Presenters will gain valuable experience and visibility while engaging with a national network of youth leaders. Participation can help strengthen communication skills, build confidence, and create opportunities for collaboration with like-minded changemakers across Canada. The event also offers a platform for youth to highlight innovative solutions that support the Sustainable Development Goals and advance positive change within their communities. Application Deadline Applications for the Goals for Tomorrow 2026 Call for Youth Presenters must be submitted by: Deadline: August 26, 2026 (11:59 PM EDT) Applicants are encouraged to apply early and prepare a compelling proposal that highlights their work, ideas, and impact. How to Apply Interested applicants can review the application guidelines and submit their proposals through the official Goals for Tomorrow application portal. Before applying, be sure to review the presentation formats, eligibility requirements, and frequently asked questions provided by the organizers. Conclusion The Goals for Tomorrow 2026 festival is more than just a speaking opportunity—it is a platform for young Canadians to share their ideas, inspire action, and contribute to shaping a more sustainable and inclusive future. Whether you are an innovator, community leader, artist, entrepreneur, researcher, activist, or changemaker, this national virtual festival offers a unique space to amplify your voice and connect with like-minded youth from across the country. By participating, presenters will gain valuable leadership and public speaking experience, expand their professional networks, and showcase projects that are creating positive social, environmental, and economic impact. The festival also provides an opportunity to engage in meaningful discussions around global citizenship, international development, and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). If you are passionate about creating change and have a story, idea, project, or initiative worth sharing, this is your chance to make an impact on a national stage. Submit your proposal before the August 26, 2026 deadline and become part of a growing movement of young leaders working to build a better tomorrow for all. title: Yale Digital Ethics Center Symposium (DECS) 2026 in USA | Fully Funded Opportunity for PhD Students and Postdoctoral Scholars
summary: The Yale Digital Ethics Center (DEC) is inviting applications for the inaugural Digital Ethics Center Symposium (DECS) 2026, a prestigious international event designed to showcase the work of emerging scholars examining the ethical, legal, social, and governance implications of digital technologies. Taking place on October 16, 2026, at Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut, the symposium offers PhD students and postdoctoral researchers a unique platform to present their work, engage with leading scholars, and contribute to critical discussions shaping the future of digital governance and ethics. Selected participants will receive fully funded travel support, accommodation, recognition through the inaugural DECS Best Paper Award, and opportunities for future collaboration with Yale’s Digital Ethics Center. About the Digital Ethics Center Symposium (DECS) The Digital Ethics Center Symposium is a new international academic forum established by Yale University s Digital Ethics Center to support early-career researchers whose work explores the ethical and human dimensions of digital transformation. The symposium focuses on the Governance, Ethical, Legal, and Social Implications (GELSI) of digital technologies and seeks to foster meaningful dialogue between emerging scholars and established experts in the field. Participants will present peer-reviewed papers and receive detailed commentary from Digital Ethics Center researchers, followed by scholarly discussion and feedback. Symposium Theme DECS 2026 welcomes research that examines the governance and societal implications of digital technologies, including topics related to: • Digital ethics • Artificial intelligence governance • Technology policy • Data ethics • Privacy and surveillance • Algorithmic accountability • Responsible innovation • Human-centered technology • Digital rights and regulation • Ethical dimensions of emerging technologies The symposium particularly encourages work that can inform policy development and governance frameworks across different jurisdictions. Benefits of Participation Selected presenters will receive: • Full round-trip travel support to New Haven, Connecticut • Two nights of accommodation • The inaugural DECS Best Paper Award medal • An invitation to collaborate with Professor Luciano Floridi and Digital Ethics Center researchers during the Spring 2027 semester • Opportunities to receive feedback from leading scholars in digital ethics • International academic visibility and networking opportunities Publication Opportunity One of the most attractive features of the symposium is the publication opportunity available to applicants. All high-quality submissions including papers not selected for presentation will be considered for publication in a special issue of Philosophy Technology , a leading journal in the field. This provides an exceptional opportunity for early-career researchers to gain scholarly recognition and contribute to ongoing debates in digital ethics and technology governance. Who Can Apply? Applications are open to: • PhD students • Postdoctoral scholars Applicants from all countries are encouraged to apply. The symposium is specifically designed to support emerging researchers whose work explores the ethical and societal dimensions of digital technologies. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must ensure that: • Their submission is original work. • The paper is not formally published. • The manuscript is not currently under review elsewhere. • The manuscript is not committed for publication with another outlet. • Preprints and working papers may be submitted. • Any publicly available preprint version must be disclosed in the application. • Only one submission may be made as first author. title: Arcadia Impact AI Governance Taskforce Autumn 2026: Fully Remote Global Research Fellowship for Professionals Transitioning into AI Governance
summary: Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping industries, governments, and societies worldwide. As AI systems become increasingly powerful, the need for skilled professionals capable of developing effective governance frameworks, safety policies, and risk mitigation strategies has never been greater. To help address this growing global challenge, Arcadia Impact has opened applications for its AI Governance Taskforce Autumn 2026 Cohort , a prestigious research programme designed for experienced professionals who want to transition into frontier AI governance. This highly selective programme offers participants an opportunity to conduct policy-relevant AI governance research alongside internationally recognized experts while maintaining their current professional commitments. Running over 12 weeks on a part-time basis, the programme is fully remote and welcomes applicants from around the world. Although voluntary and unpaid, the fellowship provides invaluable exposure, professional networking opportunities, practical research experience, and a proven pathway into careers focused on AI governance, AI safety, and policy development. About the Arcadia Impact AI Governance Taskforce The AI Governance Taskforce is a specialized research programme that supports experienced professionals seeking to transition into careers focused on reducing catastrophic and systemic risks associated with transformative artificial intelligence. Unlike many AI education programmes that focus on technical development or AI ethics generally, the AI Governance Taskforce specifically concentrates on frontier AI governance . Participants work on policy-focused research designed to improve governance systems capable of addressing advanced AI risks before they become major global threats. The programme enables professionals from diverse disciplines to apply their existing expertise to one of the world s fastest-growing policy areas while receiving mentorship from leaders in AI governance and safety. Why This Programme Matters As governments, international organizations, and technology companies race to regulate increasingly advanced AI systems, there is a significant global shortage of professionals who understand both public policy and frontier AI governance. Arcadia Impact created the AI Governance Taskforce to bridge this gap by providing professionals with: Practical research experience Exposure to real-world AI governance challenges High-level mentorship Collaborative policy development experience Professional networks within the AI safety community Participants leave the programme with stronger credentials that position them for future opportunities in AI governance, research, public policy, and international organizations. Programme Overview The Autumn 2026 cohort has been carefully structured to accommodate working professionals. Programme Details Programme Duration: 12 weeks Programme Dates: 12 October 2026 – 15 January 2027 Year-End Break: Two-week holiday break between 18 December 2026 and 4 January 2027 Commitment: Approximately 8 hours per week Delivery Mode: Fully remote Location: Global Programme Type: Voluntary and unpaid Available Positions: Approximately 20 Research Associate places Participants can continue with their existing careers while contributing to meaningful AI governance research. What Participants Will Do Research Associates become members of multidisciplinary research teams composed of four individuals. Each team works closely with: A dedicated Research Team Leader A leading AI governance expert Other experienced professionals from diverse disciplines Together, they investigate pressing AI governance questions and produce policy-oriented research intended to influence real-world decision-making. Typical research outputs include: Academic-style preprint papers Policy briefs Government policy memoranda Research articles Stakeholder reports These publications are designed to address challenges surrounding advanced AI governance and catastrophic AI risks. Learn from World-Leading AI Governance Experts Participants receive direct guidance from senior practitioners working across some of the world s most respected AI safety and governance organizations. Expert partners have included professionals affiliated with: UK AI Security Institute (AISI) Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI) AI Incident Database (AIID) MIT AI Risk Initiative (AIRI) Centre for Long-Term Resilience (CLTR) SaferAI The Future Society Future of Life Institute (FLI) Leading universities and academic institutions Research Team Leaders work alongside these experts to ensure projects remain academically rigorous and policy relevant. Areas of Research Projects typically focus on governance challenges surrounding frontier AI systems. Examples include: AI incident monitoring AI governance frameworks AI safety cases International AI policy Frontier AI regulation AI risk management Open-source intelligence for AI governance Dangerous capability thresholds AI accountability mechanisms Loss-of-control scenarios International governance infrastructure Research themes evolve with emerging developments in AI governance. Outstanding Career Outcomes for Alumni One of the strongest features of the AI Governance Taskforce is its exceptional alumni network. Graduates have progressed into positions at organizations including: Google DeepMind SaferAI ControlAI Pour Demain Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative MIT AI Risk Initiative Centre for Long-Term Resilience The Future Society GovAI IAPS Future Impact Group Many alumni have also: Secured research management positions Joined international AI governance fellowships Collaborated with renowned AI researcher Yoshua Bengio Started independent AI governance initiatives Returned to the Taskforce as Research Team Leaders These achievements demonstrate the programme s effectiveness as a launchpad for careers in frontier AI governance. International Recognition of Research Research produced through the Taskforce has received significant international recognition. Achievements include: Acceptance at the International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML) Technical AI Governance Workshop Best Paper Award recognition Co-authorship opportunities with expert partners Features in Time Magazine Coverage in the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists Publication in the AI Policy Bulletin These accomplishments reflect the quality and impact of the programme s research outputs. Who Should Apply? Arcadia Impact is seeking motivated professionals who have already begun transitioning toward careers in frontier AI governance. Applicants should demonstrate genuine commitment rather than simply exploring the field. Professionals from a wide variety of disciplines are encouraged to apply, including: Law Public Policy Economics Political Science International Relations Engineering Machine Learning Software Engineering Systems Engineering Mechanical Engineering Safety Engineering Computer Science Philosophy Social Sciences Humanities Management Applicants do not need to possess deep technical AI expertise. Eligibility Requirements Applicants should be able to: Commit approximately eight hours per week throughout the programme. Work effectively within a structured remote research team. Demonstrate commitment to reducing catastrophic risks from frontier AI. Show evidence of progressing toward a career in AI governance. Communicate clearly through writing and research. Exercise sound judgement when evaluating AI governance challenges. Work independently with minimal supervision. Arcadia Impact encourages applications even from candidates who meet only part of the preferred profile. What the Selection Committee Looks For Applications are assessed using several criteria, including: 1. Motivation Candidates should demonstrate a clear commitment to transitioning into frontier AI governance. 2. Awareness of the AI Landscape Applicants should understand: Frontier AI capabilities Emerging AI risks Key organizations Existing governance initiatives 3. Transferable Expertise Professional knowledge from previous careers should be applicable to AI governance research. 4. Research Skills Strong reasoning, writing, analytical thinking, and policy research skills are highly valued. 5. Independent Initiative Candidates should show evidence of creating opportunities independently and pursuing meaningful work without needing formal structures. Application Process The Autumn 2026 selection process consists of four stages. Stage One – General Application Applicants submit: Curriculum Vitae (CV) Short written responses No writing sample is required. Stage Two – Project Application Shortlisted candidates receive: Project briefs A short written task related to their preferred project Stage Three – Interview Successful applicants participate in an online interview where they discuss: Motivation Experience Research interests Career goals Stage Four – Offers Selected candidates receive offers to join a specific research team. Approximately 20 Research Associate positions will be available. Important Dates Applicants should carefully note the following timeline: Activity Date Applications Open 5 August 2026 General Application Deadline 31 August 2026 (Anywhere on Earth) Stage Two Invitations By 7 September 2026 Project Applications Due 13 September 2026 Interview Invitations 21 September 2026 Interviews Late September 2026 Offers Issued Week commencing 5 October 2026 Programme Begins 12 October 2026 Programme Ends 15 January 2027 Why You Should Apply Although the programme is unpaid, participants receive benefits that can significantly accelerate careers in AI governance. These include: Working directly with internationally recognized AI governance experts Building a strong professional network Producing publishable policy research Strengthening research credentials Gaining exposure to real-world AI governance challenges Improving opportunities for future fellowships and employment Collaborating with professionals from multiple disciplines Contributing to research that influences AI policy discussions worldwide For professionals committed to shaping the future of AI governance, this represents an exceptional learning and career development opportunity. How to Apply Interested candidates should submit their application through the official Arcadia Impact application portal before the deadline. Applicants with questions about the programme may contact: Ben R Smith Taskforce Lead Email: ben [at] arcadiaimpact [dot] org APPLY HERE Application Deadline Applications close at 23:59 Anywhere on Earth (AoE) on Monday, 31 August 2026 (12:59 BST on Tuesday, 1 September 2026). Visit HERE to learn more about the Arcadia Impact AI Governance Taskforce Autumn 2026. Conclusion The Arcadia Impact AI Governance Taskforce Autumn 2026 Cohort offers an outstanding opportunity for experienced professionals who want to transition into one of the world s most important emerging fields. Through expert mentorship, collaborative research, international networking, and hands-on policy development, participants gain the experience and credibility needed to contribute meaningfully to frontier AI governance. Whether your background is in law, engineering, public policy, economics, philosophy, political science, or another discipline, this programme provides a structured pathway into AI governance while allowing you to continue your current professional commitments. Given the programme s strong alumni outcomes and international recognition, professionals interested in shaping the future governance of transformative AI should strongly consider applying. title: Free Net Zero Learning Pathway by UN SDG:Learn | Learn Climate Action and Science-Based Targets
summary: Are you interested in climate action, sustainability, and achieving a net-zero future? The UN SDG:Learn Net Zero Learning Pathway offers a free opportunity for learners worldwide to develop a comprehensive understanding of net-zero emissions, climate science, and science-based targets. Developed through collaboration with leading United Nations partners, this self-paced learning pathway helps individuals, professionals, students, policymakers, and organizations understand how to align climate actions with global goals and contribute to a more sustainable future. The pathway combines three specialized courses that guide learners from foundational concepts to practical implementation of net-zero strategies. About the Net Zero Learning Pathway The Net Zero Learning Pathway introduces participants to the science behind climate change, the importance of achieving net-zero emissions, and the frameworks used by organizations worldwide to set and achieve climate goals. Through a structured learning journey, participants will: • Understand the fundamentals of net-zero emissions. • Learn why climate action is critical for sustainable development. • Explore practical approaches to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. • Understand science-based target methodologies. • Learn how organizations align climate commitments with the 1.5°C pathway. • Gain knowledge of internationally recognized net-zero standards. The pathway is completely online and self-paced, allowing learners to study at their convenience. What You Will Learn The learning pathway is divided into three modules that progressively build climate knowledge and practical skills. Module 1 : Understanding Net Zero Course 1 : The Net-Zero Standard Provider : United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) This course introduces learners to the concept of net-zero emissions and explains why reaching net zero is essential for addressing climate change. Participants will explore: • Climate science fundamentals. • The role of net-zero strategies in limiting global warming. • Key concepts and terminology related to net-zero commitments. • Practical actions that organizations and individuals can take to reduce emissions. This course provides the foundation needed to understand broader climate action frameworks. Module 2 : Science-Based Targets for Net Zero Course 2 : Net Zero 101: What, Why and How Provider :United Nations University (UNU) This introductory course examines the importance of net-zero commitments and provides practical guidance on how organizations can contribute to global climate goals. Participants will learn: • What net zero means in practice. • Why net-zero commitments matter. • How emissions reductions contribute to climate mitigation. • Key approaches for implementing climate strategies. • The relationship between sustainability and long-term resilience. The course is ideal for individuals seeking a broader understanding of climate solutions and net-zero implementation. Module 3: The Net-Zero Standard in Practice Course 3 : Setting Science-Based Targets to Achieve Net-Zero Provider : United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) This advanced course focuses on helping organizations establish science-based targets that align with global climate objectives. Participants will explore: • Science-based target methodologies. • Setting near-term and long-term emissions reduction goals. • Aligning organizational targets with the 1.5°C climate pathway. • Best practices for implementing the Net-Zero Standard. • Strategies for measuring and tracking climate progress. This course is particularly valuable for sustainability professionals, business leaders, policymakers, and organizations seeking to strengthen their climate commitments. Who Should Enroll? The Net Zero Learning Pathway is suitable for: • Students and young professionals. • Climate and sustainability advocates. • Environmental practitioners. • Corporate sustainability teams. • Government officials and policymakers. • NGO professionals. • Researchers and academics. • Anyone interested in climate action and sustainable development. No prior experience is required to begin the pathway. Benefits of the Learning Pathway Participants will benefit from: • Free access to high-quality United Nations learning resources. • Flexible self-paced learning. • Expert insights from leading global institutions. • Practical knowledge on climate action and net-zero implementation. • Skills relevant to sustainability and environmental careers. • Increased understanding of science-based climate targets. • Enhanced capacity to contribute to organizational and community climate initiatives. Why Net Zero Matters Net-zero emissions have become a central goal in global efforts to combat climate change. Governments, businesses, institutions, and communities worldwide are adopting net-zero commitments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and limit global warming. Understanding how net-zero frameworks operate and how science-based targets are established is increasingly important for professionals working in sustainability, environmental management, policy development, and corporate responsibility. This learning pathway provides a valuable opportunity to gain these critical skills at no cost. Conclusion The UN SDG:Learn Net Zero Learning Pathway offers a comprehensive and accessible introduction to climate action, net-zero standards, and science-based targets. Through three expertly designed courses from the United Nations Global Compact and United Nations University , learners can build the knowledge and practical skills needed to support a sustainable, low-carbon future. Whether you are a student, sustainability professional, policymaker, or simply passionate about climate action, this free learning opportunity can help you better understand the pathways toward achieving global climate goals and creating meaningful environmental impact. title: DAAD Young Ambassadors 2027 Applications Open: Represent Germany, Inspire Future Scholars, and Promote International Education
summary: Germany has long been recognized as one of the world s leading destinations for higher education, research, and academic innovation. Every year, thousands of international students choose German universities and research institutions because of their world-class education, cutting-edge research opportunities, affordable study options, and vibrant multicultural environment. To encourage more students to explore these opportunities, the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) has officially opened applications for the DAAD Young Ambassadors 2027 Programme . This unique initiative is designed for enthusiastic alumni and current students who have studied or conducted research in Germany and are passionate about sharing their experiences with others. The programme offers participants an opportunity to become official representatives of German higher education in their home countries by promoting study and research opportunities through presentations, outreach activities, educational events, and student engagement initiatives. If your time in Germany transformed your academic or professional journey and you are eager to motivate others to pursue similar opportunities, this programme provides the perfect platform to make an impact. What is the DAAD Young Ambassadors Programme? The DAAD Young Ambassadors Programme is an outreach initiative organized by the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD). The programme brings together former and current international students and researchers who have firsthand experience studying in Germany. Rather than serving as a traditional scholarship, the programme focuses on educational outreach and peer-to-peer engagement. Selected ambassadors use their personal experiences to educate prospective students about studying and conducting research in Germany. Young Ambassadors become trusted voices who can answer questions, share practical insights, and encourage talented students to consider Germany as a destination for higher education. Through presentations, educational fairs, seminars, university events, and other awareness activities, ambassadors help bridge the information gap between prospective applicants and German institutions. Why Germany? Germany continues to rank among the world s most attractive study destinations due to numerous academic and professional advantages. Some of these include: Internationally recognized universities High-quality education Strong research infrastructure Numerous English-taught programmes Affordable or tuition-free education at many public universities Excellent career opportunities Strong links between academia and industry Rich cultural diversity Global networking opportunities The Young Ambassadors Programme helps communicate these benefits through individuals who have personally experienced studying or researching in Germany. Purpose of the DAAD Young Ambassadors Programme The programme aims to: Promote Germany as a preferred destination for higher education. Increase awareness of German universities and research institutions. Encourage talented students to pursue international education. Share authentic experiences from former and current students. Strengthen educational cooperation between Germany and participating countries. Build a network of motivated education ambassadors. Inspire future applicants through peer engagement. What Will DAAD Young Ambassadors Do? Selected ambassadors will actively participate in promoting educational opportunities in Germany. Typical responsibilities include: 1. Sharing Personal Experiences Participants explain: Their academic journey Student life in Germany Research experiences Cultural experiences Career development after studying in Germany These firsthand stories help prospective students better understand what studying in Germany is truly like. 2. Conducting Presentations Young Ambassadors organize or participate in presentations at: Universities Colleges Schools Career fairs Education expos Information sessions These presentations introduce students to: German universities Study programmes Scholarships Research opportunities Student life Application processes 3. Participating in Educational Events Ambassadors represent DAAD during various outreach events, including: Study abroad fairs Information seminars Educational exhibitions University outreach programmes Student networking sessions 4. Inspiring Future Students A key objective is encouraging talented students to pursue academic opportunities in Germany by providing reliable information and practical advice. Who Can Apply? DAAD welcomes applications from motivated individuals who meet all eligibility requirements. Applicants must: Be nationals of India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, or Sri Lanka. Have studied or currently be studying or conducting research at a German institution. Be below 32 years of age as of 1 January 2027 . Be enthusiastic about promoting Germany through educational presentations or events. Be willing and able to participate in the online Young Ambassadors Training Workshop scheduled for November 2026 . Meeting all eligibility criteria is essential for consideration. Age Requirement Applicants must be: Under 32 years of age as of 1 January 2027 . This age requirement ensures the programme engages young professionals and recent academic participants who can effectively connect with prospective students. Previous German Study or Research Experience Applicants must have direct academic or research experience in Germany. Eligible individuals include those who: Previously studied at a German university. Are currently studying in Germany. Previously conducted research in Germany. Are currently conducting research at a German institution. Having firsthand experience enables ambassadors to provide authentic guidance to prospective applicants. Passion for Educational Outreach Academic qualifications alone are not sufficient. DAAD is looking for individuals who are: Passionate about Germany Excellent communicators Motivated to inspire others Comfortable speaking publicly Interested in educational outreach Willing to organize presentations and events Communication skills and enthusiasm play an important role in becoming an effective ambassador. Mandatory Training Workshop Successful applicants must participate in the online Young Ambassadors Training Workshop scheduled for November 2026 . The training prepares ambassadors by providing guidance on: Programme objectives Outreach strategies Presentation techniques Communication skills Promotional activities Representing DAAD professionally Attendance is mandatory. Benefits of Becoming a DAAD Young Ambassador Although this is not a scholarship programme, selected ambassadors receive valuable professional and personal development opportunities. These include: Leadership Development Participants strengthen their leadership abilities through educational outreach and public engagement. Public Speaking Experience Ambassadors gain confidence by delivering presentations and interacting with diverse audiences. Networking Opportunities Participants become part of a growing network of: DAAD representatives German institutions Education professionals Fellow ambassadors Students International Exposure The programme strengthens participants international profile while maintaining connections with Germany s academic community. Professional Recognition Serving as a DAAD Young Ambassador demonstrates commitment to international education and community engagement, enhancing professional credentials. Opportunity to Inspire Others Perhaps the greatest reward is helping future students access life-changing educational opportunities in Germany. Why Your Experience Matters Students often trust advice from peers who have already experienced studying abroad. By sharing practical experiences about: Student life Academic expectations Cultural adjustment Living costs Research opportunities Campus experiences Career development Young Ambassadors help prospective applicants make informed decisions and prepare for successful study experiences in Germany. Application Deadline Interested applicants must submit their applications before: Deadline: 30 September 2026 Late applications may not be considered, so prospective ambassadors are encouraged to apply well before the closing date. How to Apply Eligible applicants should complete the official online application through the DAAD application portal before the deadline. Applicants are encouraged to carefully review all eligibility requirements and prepare any necessary supporting information before submitting their applications. APPLY HERE Why You Should Apply If your academic journey in Germany has positively influenced your education, career, or personal growth, becoming a DAAD Young Ambassador offers an opportunity to give back. By joining this programme, you can: Inspire future generations of students. Promote international education. Share valuable academic experiences. Develop leadership and communication skills. Expand your professional network. Continue contributing to Germany s global academic community. For motivated young professionals and students who enjoy mentoring others, this programme represents an excellent opportunity to make a lasting educational impact. Visit HERE for more information about the DAAD Young Ambassadors 2027 programme. Conclusion The DAAD Young Ambassadors 2027 Programme provides a meaningful opportunity for former and current students and researchers with German academic experience to become advocates for international education. Through presentations, outreach activities, and educational events, ambassadors play an important role in encouraging talented students to explore Germany s outstanding universities and research institutions. Beyond promoting study opportunities, the programme also helps participants strengthen their leadership, communication, and networking skills while remaining connected to the German academic community. If you meet the eligibility criteria and are passionate about sharing your educational journey, this is an excellent opportunity to inspire future scholars and contribute to international academic cooperation. Remember to submit your application before the 30 September 2026 deadline to be considered for the 2027 cohort. For more global Fellowship opportunities, visit OFY HERE. title: Chief Programs & Partnerships Officer at Women for Women International (WfWI): Global Executive Leadership Opportunity Across Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and the United States
summary: Women for Women International (WfWI) is inviting experienced global development leaders to apply for the position of Chief Programs Partnerships Officer (CPPO) . This permanent executive leadership role offers an exceptional opportunity to shape the future of one of the world s leading organizations dedicated to supporting women survivors of war and conflict. The successful candidate will join WfWI s Executive Leadership Team and play a central role in defining the organization s global program strategy, strengthening institutional partnerships, ensuring program quality, guiding evidence-based decision-making, and leading global business development initiatives. The position is available to professionals who already possess the legal right to work in one of the approved countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Rwanda, South Africa, Nigeria, Iraq, Germany, the United Kingdom, or the United States. This role is ideal for highly accomplished international development professionals with extensive experience leading complex humanitarian and development programs across multiple countries, particularly within fragile and conflict-affected settings. About Women for Women International Women for Women International (WfWI) is a globally recognized nonprofit organization committed to empowering women who have survived war, armed conflict, and humanitarian crises. Since its founding in 1993, the organization has supported more than 550,000 women across 17 conflict-affected countries , helping them rebuild their lives through economic empowerment, education, rights awareness, health information, and community leadership. WfWI currently works in countries including: Afghanistan Bosnia and Herzegovina Democratic Republic of the Congo Iraq Kosovo Nigeria Rwanda South Sudan Through its flagship Stronger Women, Stronger Nations Programme , participants gain: Livelihood and vocational skills Financial literacy Savings and income-generation knowledge Leadership development Women s rights education Health awareness Community support networks The organization believes that empowering women creates stronger families, stronger communities, and ultimately more peaceful societies. Position Overview Position: Chief Programs Partnerships Officer (CPPO) Department: Global Programs Unit Employment Type: Full-time Contract: Permanent / Open-ended Leadership Grade: L Reports To: International Chief Executive Officer Work Arrangement: Remote or Hybrid (depending on location) Eligible Work Locations Applicants must already have legal authorization to work in one of the following countries: Ghana Kenya Rwanda South Africa Nigeria Iraq Germany United Kingdom United States Women for Women International does not sponsor work visas and does not provide relocation support . An Executive Leadership Role with Global Impact The Chief Programs Partnerships Officer serves as one of the most senior executives within Women for Women International. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the CPPO helps shape the organization s future by ensuring that every program remains: Mission-driven Evidence-based Financially sustainable Operationally feasible Centered on women s needs Responsive to changing humanitarian contexts The role serves as the International CEO s principal strategic advisor on matters involving: Global program strategy Organizational growth Geographic expansion Institutional partnerships Program coherence Funding alignment Delivery continuity Rather than directly managing all country offices permanently, the CPPO provides strategic oversight through a matrix leadership structure that ensures consistent program quality across regions. Responsibilities include: Leading the development of WfWI s global program strategy Ensuring all programs remain evidence-informed Improving program quality worldwide Designing innovative interventions Maintaining global technical standards Establishing quality assurance systems Aligning all programming with organizational strategy The successful candidate will ensure that every country program delivers meaningful impact while remaining operationally realistic. 2.
