This includes: Working closely with Regional Directors Supporting Country Directors Monitoring delivery quality Reviewing annual country plans Assessing implementation risks Supporting organizational transitions Maintaining strong technical oversight The CPPO will ensure that local implementation aligns with global organizational standards. 3. Guide Program Design and Innovation The executive will oversee technical teams responsible for: Program Design Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning (MERL) Country Office Support Grant Management Program Planning Key duties include: Approving new program models Reviewing innovations Supporting research initiatives Strengthening evidence generation Promoting data-driven decision-making Improving operational efficiency Ensuring scalability of interventions 4. Lead the Crisis Response Fund The CPPO serves as Executive Sponsor of WfWI s Crisis Response Fund. Key responsibilities include: Chairing the Steering Committee Approving funding allocations Reviewing high-risk partnerships Supporting emergency interventions Managing conflict-response strategies Ensuring safeguarding compliance Coordinating fundraising for crisis programming This work enables WfWI to support women in countries where it may not yet maintain permanent offices. 5. Oversee Business Development An important part of the role involves leading institutional fundraising and strategic partnerships. Responsibilities include: Guiding the Global Business Development Unit Developing fundraising strategies Reviewing institutional proposals Managing donor relationships Evaluating funding opportunities Approving major grants Ensuring funding aligns with organizational priorities The CPPO has final authority over significant programmatic funding decisions. 6. Build Strategic Global Partnerships The successful executive will represent WfWI internationally. Potential partners include: Governments Bilateral agencies Multilateral organizations Universities Research institutions Think tanks International NGOs Philanthropic organizations Strategic networks The CPPO will strengthen partnerships that enhance both organizational impact and long-term sustainability. 7. Organizational Leadership As a senior executive, the CPPO will: Lead high-performing international teams Supervise senior global managers Manage large budgets Present to Executive Leadership Engage with Board committees Support organizational transformation Clarify governance structures Strengthen cross-functional collaboration Leadership Responsibilities The CPPO directly supervises: Deputy Chief Programs Partnerships Officer Global Director of Business Development Crisis Response Fund Manager Global Programs Unit Coordinator During organizational transition periods, designated Country Directors may also report directly to the CPPO. Collaboration Across the Organization The role requires close collaboration with multiple senior leaders. These include: Chief Executive Officer Supporting strategic organizational decisions and global growth. Chief Operating Officer Coordinating: Operations Procurement Finance Compliance Risk Management Security Human Resources Information Technology Chief Research, Policy, Advocacy Strategic Communications Officer Working together to ensure that: Communications reflect evidence Advocacy is informed by field realities Research influences programming Organizational messaging remains credible Required Qualifications Applicants should possess: A Master s degree in International Development, Social Sciences, Gender Studies, Humanitarian Studies, Public Policy, or a closely related discipline. At least 15 years of senior leadership experience in international development, humanitarian action, or nonprofit management. Extensive experience managing complex international program portfolios. Proven leadership in fragile and conflict-affected environments. Strong expertise in program strategy and organizational transformation. Significant experience in institutional fundraising and donor engagement. Experience managing geographically dispersed international teams. Strong strategic planning capabilities. Excellent stakeholder management skills. Deep understanding of gender equality and women s rights. Ability to work effectively within complex matrix organizations. Existing legal authorization to work in one of the listed countries. Preferred Qualifications Women for Women International would particularly value candidates who have: International leadership experience across multiple regions. Experience working in Africa and the Middle East. Strong donor and institutional networks. Experience leading research and evaluation initiatives. Knowledge of localization approaches. Experience with integrated multi-sector programming. Expertise in partnership-driven development models. Skills That Will Make Candidates Competitive Ideal applicants should demonstrate: Executive leadership Strategic vision Change management Program management Business development Partnership building Team leadership Financial oversight Communication Decision-making Negotiation Evidence-based planning Cross-cultural leadership Risk management Innovation management Benefits Women for Women International offers a competitive employment package that includes: Competitive location-adjusted salary Permanent employment Remote or hybrid work options depending on location Additional location-specific benefits Opportunity to lead global humanitarian programming Executive-level leadership experience International collaboration Significant influence on global women s empowerment initiatives Organizational Values Employees are expected to uphold WfWI s core values: Empowerment Integrity Respect Resilience Leadership principles include: Decisive Accountable Courageous Adaptable Inclusive All staff must comply with the organization s Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policies. Applications are welcomed regardless of: Age Disability Gender identity Race Religion Sexual orientation Marital status Political opinion Pregnancy or maternity status The organization believes that diverse teams strengthen innovation, collaboration, and organizational performance. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the successful candidate will shape organizational strategy, strengthen institutional partnerships, oversee high-impact programs, and ensure that WfWI continues to deliver evidence-based, women-centered interventions across conflict-affected regions. This executive role is particularly suited to leaders with extensive experience in international development, humanitarian response, gender equality, strategic fundraising, and organizational transformation. Those who are passionate about advancing women s rights, building resilient communities, and driving meaningful global impact will find this to be a highly rewarding career opportunity.
